body.en:
Question B-002-004-001.

Why the correct answer is right: Listening before transmitting protects contacts already in progress and prevents you from doubling with stations you did not know were there.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "Check your antenna for resonance at the selected frequency": Antenna resonance matters to station setup, but it is not the first shared-channel action before every transmission.
- sourceIndex 2: "Make sure the SWR on your transmission line is high enough": High SWR is not desirable, and checking it is not a substitute for listening to the frequency.
- sourceIndex 3: "Increase power to ensure someone will hear you": Increasing power before listening can make interference worse rather than prevent it.
